term: being able to be without another (CanBeWithout y x)
definition: CanBeWithout y x: y can be while x is not. It is the relation in the criterion of natural priority 'quae possunt esse sine aliis et illa non possunt esse sine eis' (Aquinas, In V Metaph. lect. 13 n. 15, pinned passage AQUINAS-IN-METAPH-V-L13), 'possunt' read as real possibility. Example: the sun can be without the lit air. Non-example: the lit air cannot be without the sun. It is a modal relation, distinct from the counterfactual DependsForBeing (DEF-DEPENDS-FOR-BEING); two open premises (STMT-DEPENDENCE-EXCLUDES-BEING-WITHOUT, STMT-INDEPENDENCE-ALLOWS-BEING-WITHOUT) relate them. No structural property is built in.
note: Stipulative reading of the pinned In V Metaph. lect. 13 passage; no claim is made on it (attribution deferred). A claim on n. 15 would source it.
